title: hello-multichat — one daemon, three chat surfaces (target: channel)

beats.label: Open the starter README
beats.cue: “One daemon listens on Slack, Telegram, AND Discord simultaneously.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed crewhaus.yaml stays untouched.

beats.label: Load the keys
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — a model key plus at least one platform's credentials.

verify.note: operator-supplied demos/.env; channel tokens are per-platform

groups.title: Beat 1 · The spec — an assistant that meets you where you are

beats.label: The header: what it's for
beats.cue: A local-first, always-on assistant that reaches you on whichever surface is convenient — and a header that names all eight env vars, of which “at minimum one channel's creds must be set.”

beats.label: Name it, pick the shape
beats.cue: target: channel — this compiles to a long-running daemon, not a REPL you sit in front of.

beats.label: The model and the voice
beats.cue: “One sentence is usually the right length.” No preambles, and mirror the user's register.

beats.label: Classify every inbound message
beats.cue: Five buckets — chat, lookup, task, approval, status — and the three that need machinery get an explicit route: planner, web-plus-citations, or just answer.

beats.label: The rules it answers under
beats.cue: Ask before anything destructive, never fabricate, and don't pretend to be a coding agent.

beats.label: Three tools
beats.cue: A daemon strangers can message gets the smallest tool belt that still does the job.

beats.label: Add the planner sub-agent
beats.cue: Multi-step work gets a 3–5 step plan first. The planner plans and executes nothing.

beats.label: Three surfaces, one thread key
beats.cue: Slack, Telegram, Discord — acked with 👀 wherever the platform has a reaction API, and sessionKey: thread keeps every conversation its own session.

beats.label: Let it wake itself
beats.cue: Every 2h a fresh synthetic session fires, reads HEARTBEAT.md, and takes at most one action.

beats.label: Open the heartbeat playbook
beats.cue: “The default verdict on every tick is silence.” Editable prose, not code — tune it for your life.

beats.label: Give the operator a window
beats.cue: A control-UI listener on 19001: /status as JSON, a dashboard at the root.

beats.label: Leave the connectors commented
beats.cue: This is the extension point: uncomment a block and your calendar, mail or files show up as tools.

beats.label: Permissions: mode default, and why
beats.cue: A channel daemon has nobody to prompt, so `ask` converts to `deny`. Read, search, fetch, dispatch.

beats.label: Refuse the host shell
beats.cue: “A random user in any of these channels should NOT be able to run shell commands on your machine.”

beats.label: Hand compaction to Haiku
beats.cue: Older turns get summarised per session, so a thread that runs for weeks stays cheap.

beats.label: Lint the spec
beats.cue: “lint: clean — no findings.” Parse, the IR passes, and the tool-scope audit.

beats.label: Lower the spec to IR
beats.cue: “The spec is sugar; this JSON is what the compiler actually sees.” Redirect it — 189 lines of YAML become 127 lines of IR, which reads better in the editor than in scrollback.

verify.note: 127-line IR written to the scratch dir; the next beat opens it

beats.label: Open the IR
beats.cue: Every block of the ladder, lowered and named: channels, routing, permissions, subAgents, compaction, continuity, heartbeat, gateway.

beats.label: Project it as an agent loop
beats.cue: Perceive is three channel ingresses plus a heartbeat timer — and nothing checks output before it ships.

verify.note: read-only projection; reports no in-loop evaluation and no budget:

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: GREEN with no key: shape asserted, deps installed, booted as far as its env refs allow.

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the spec env refs gate

beats.label: Open the emitted daemon
beats.cue: Four programs out of one YAML: the daemon, the gateway, the session router, the agent.

beats.label: Try crewhaus run
beats.cue: “run supports target cli or browser” — a channel daemon is compile-only. The bundle is the runtime.

verify.note: deliberate rejection, exit 1: run drives cli|browser; other shapes are compile-only

beats.label: Ask what it would check
beats.cue: Three surfaces, three preflight probes — auth.test, getWebhookInfo, applications/@me — printed before a single one is made.

verify.note: prints the would-call plan for all three platforms, secrets redacted; no network, reads no token

beats.label: Ask what it still needs
beats.cue: Scrub the credentials and the daemon names all seven platform vars plus the model key — before it opens a socket. Designed refusal, exit 2.
beats.command: env -u SLACK_BOT_TOKEN -u SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET -u TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN -u TELEGRAM_SECRET_TOKEN -u DISCORD_APP_ID -u DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN -u DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY -u ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY bun live/dist/daemon.ts

verify.note: the env -u list is required: Setup already sourced .env into this same terminal. `[daemon] missing required env vars: SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_SECRET_TOKEN, DISCORD_APP_ID, DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN, DISCORD_PUBLIC_KEY, ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`

beats.label: Point the platforms at one origin
beats.cue: One base URL → a Slack manifest you paste into api.slack.com once, Telegram's setWebhook, Discord's interactions endpoint. Dry run prints all three and writes nothing.

verify.note: dry run: Slack is manifest-plus-console-steps (no --apply — Slack's manifest API needs an app configuration token), Telegram is a setWebhook POST, Discord a PATCH applications/@me. The live form writes slack-app-manifest.yaml into cwd and exits 1 without all four Telegram+Discord vars

beats.label: Verify against the real platforms
beats.cue: [needs-key] Same command without --dry-run: three live probes across three platforms — exit 1 the moment one token or endpoint is wrong.

verify.note: hits slack.com, api.telegram.org and discord.com with the spec's tokens; exit 0 only when every check passes

beats.label: Boot the daemon
beats.cue: [needs-key] Backgrounded, so this same terminal can drive it. It listens forever — no “open a terminal, start a chat” ceremony.

verify.note: long-running; needs a model key and all seven platform vars (the gate beat above lists them). `&` keeps the terminal free for the beats after it

beats.label: Check daemon health
beats.cue: [needs-key] Channels, turn counts, heartbeat ticks — as JSON, from the gateway you specced.

verify.note: reads the gateway the backgrounded daemon serves on 19001

beats.label: Open the operator dashboard
beats.cue: [manual] The same numbers as a page, at the root of port 19001.

verify.note: browser view of the running daemon; macOS `open` — any browser works

beats.label: Stop the daemon
beats.cue: [needs-key] Job %1 is the daemon we backgrounded — release port 19001 so the next take starts clean.

verify.note: job %1 is the daemon run-daemon backgrounded; a fresh shell has no such job

groups.title: One more thing · the parts that aren't YAML

beats.label: Open the voice skill
beats.cue: Auto-discovered from .crewhaus/skills/ — its trigger is “*”, so it loads on every reply.

beats.label: Open the approval skill
beats.cue: For MCP tools the permission engine can't fence, the convention is written down and loadable.

beats.label: Open the heartbeat skill
beats.cue: The decision framework the heartbeat instructions name by skill id — “the default verdict on a heartbeat is silence.”

beats.label: The heartbeat is real code, not a promise
beats.cue: The spec's `every: 2h` became a setInterval in the emitted daemon — a synthetic session on a timer, logged like any other turn.

verify.note: hits include `setInterval`, `[heartbeat] tick #`, and `[heartbeat] enabled every 7200000ms` — the code behind the skill the beat before this one opened

beats.label: Count the spec
beats.cue: Three surfaces, a planner, a heartbeat, a gateway and compaction — this is the whole file.

verify.note: the committed spec, comments and all
